content: This medication is a penicillin-type antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections. It is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. How to Use: Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor, typically once daily, within one hour of finishing a meal. Swallow the tablets whole; do not crush or chew them. For optimal results, take the antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Rarely, it may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. A mild rash is a common side effect of amoxicillin and is usually not serious, but it can sometimes be difficult to distinguish from a rare rash that may indicate a severe allergic reaction. Precautions: Before taking amoxicillin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, penicillin, cephalosporin antibiotics, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Amoxicillin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, as it passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, such as some diabetic urine tests, potentially causing false results. Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. Prolonged treatment may require lab tests to monitor kidney and liver function or complete blood counts. Keep all medical and lab appointments. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
